brief: Every lit window in the town switches on in the same frame and off in the same frame. drawWindow() decides `lit` as `nightF > 0.3 && hash(sa*3, sb*7+day) > 0.42`, so roughly 58% of windows burn from dusk to dawn and nobody in this town goes to bed. Give each window its own hour: over a night the lit set should thin — early sleepers out by mid-evening, a few burning into the small hours, one or two coming on before dawn — so that 22.00 and 03.00 are visibly different pictures. Sky is ten iterations back and Sky x Polish is marked saturated; this is the deepening the domain actually wants. NOTE: this brief was issued at #34 and consumed by a harness fault before any worker ran (see b38) — there is no prior attempt to read.
successLooksLike: A filmstrip cropped to the buildings across one night shows the lit count falling from an evening peak to a small-hours floor and lifting again before dawn, with no frame in which more than a couple of windows change at once. At nightF <= 0.3 nothing is lit, exactly as now, and the daytime frame is byte-identical to HEAD.
avoid: LIT[] feeds the night glow pass — one predicate, one definition: whatever decides `lit` must be the same thing that pushes into LIT, or the glow and the pane disagree and only a crop will show it. Per-window variance comes from hash(), never R(): this runs in the renderer, and the renderer draws from the seeded stream. Match the grain — a window here is addressed per BUILDING per DAY, so a per-cell term is a silent no-op across a facade. And do not make it a second global scalar with a threshold; that is the switch you are replacing.
